entities.summary: Armand du Paty de Clam was a French army officer and amateur graphologist who played a key role in the Dreyfus affair, a major scandal that exposed anti-Semitism in the French military and government. De Clam's involvement in the affair was sparked by his work with graphology, a pseudoscientific method of analyzing handwriting to determine personality traits and character. He was accused of being a Dreyfusard, a supporter of Jewish defendant Alfred Dreyfus, who was wrongly accused of treason in 1894. De Clam's connections to the military and his expertise in graphology made him a key figure in the affair, and his involvement helped to galvanize public opinion against the military's treatment of Dreyfus. The Dreyfus affair had far-reaching consequences, including the eventual exoneration of Dreyfus and the exposure of widespread anti-Semitism in the French military and government. De Clam's legacy is complex, reflecting both the anti-Semitic attitudes of the time and his own role in highlighting these issues. In the aftermath of the Dreyfus affair, de Clam was hailed as a hero for his advocacy on behalf of Dreyfus, and his involvement in the affair is still remembered today as a pivotal moment in the struggle for Jewish rights in France.
